submitter: bugfix_357_component_identity lane — a page_components row's identity, bytes and content_data are written and carried as one bundle and no seam asserts they agree. 22 live rows name the shared `hero` component while storing a whole interactive tool; newest born 2026-08-22 on a site homepage. Successor to bugs_closed/277, whose lane's closing handoff routed here.
rationale:
A tool/game page's HTML is one `<div class="tool-page">` fragment with no `<section>` element. saveSectionsExtractFromHTML's documented fallback stores it as ONE section named "section" — the sentinel meaning IDENTITY UNKNOWN. enrichSectionsWithPlannedNames then replaces that sentinel with planned[Position-1] read from pages.sections, and `hero` is planned first on all 22 affected pages, so the tool is named `hero` purely by position. enrichSectionsWithComponentIDs resolves the name to the shared hero UUID and the single INSERT persists slot_name='hero' + component_id=<hero> + rendered_html=<the whole tool>. The sentinel for 'I do not know what this is' is converted into a confident wrong answer.

It is NOT historical: the writer is settled by row fingerprint (all 22 carry content_brief.section_guidance='hero section' and position=1, and save_page_sections_action.go is the only page_components writer that writes content_brief at all), and the newest row was created 2026-08-22 08:50:12 on vetcomparison.uk's HOMEPAGE, which now serves `class="tool-page"` where its hero should be and `data-component="hero"` zero times.

And it is self-renewing, which is why this is a flow fix and not a data repair. RerenderPageSectionsAction renders a fresh hero title band for the hero slot; the save's Layer 2 interactive carry-forward then detects that the stored row for that slot is interactive while the incoming content is not, and splices the STORED TOOL BYTES and STORED hero content_data back into the section that still carries the hero identity (save_page_sections_action.go:522-535, whose own comment says 'e.g. the hero regenerated as plain text'). The mechanism that PROTECTS the tool from being blanked is the same mechanism that PERPETUATES the mislabelling. Measured: vetcomparison.uk index has six completed rerenders 08-19..08-22 and the tool serves throughout; its rows were re-created INSIDE the 08:44:51->08:50:19 window.

I want to record a retraction, because it changes the shape of the fix. I first claimed the 13 rows carrying a full hero content_data were 'already armed' — one rebuild from having the tool replaced by a title band. That is REFUTED by the six rerenders above and is logged in WRONG_CALLS.md. Nothing here rests on it.

The discriminator is measured, not guessed. 357's own fix candidate 2 warns a birth guard must be censused first because the static-template-prefix test also fires on legitimate template drift: it flags 158 rows fleet-wide and is unusable at a refusal seam. Testing the component's OWN self-declaration instead — the data-component attribute, which saveSectionsExtractFromHTML already trusts as the identity carrier in this same file — gives 1,550 rows agreeing, 0 both-declared disagreements, and 27 flagged. The 1,550 agreements are the demand control: the predicate could have come out otherwise and did, 1,550 times. Of the 27, THREE are legitimate (loancash.co.uk verbatim pages: rebuild_policy='owned', exactly one component row, content_data->>'deploy_mode'='verbatim' — they store a full document because that is what a verbatim page IS), so the guard carries a verbatim exemption and the genuine set is 24. I originally reported 'zero false positives' having not opened those rows; that is corrected here and logged.

plan.summary: Type the fallback row at birth instead of naming it positionally (Layer A); verify identity against the bytes at the ONE INSERT every composition path flows through, recording always at Error level and refusing only behind an opt-in field defaulting OFF (Layer B); and detect the class fleet-wide across all six page_components writers with a discovery check filing the same typed item (Layer D). This is bugs_open/342's OWN STATED NEXT STEP, not a departure from it: 342 shipped report-only at the adjacent render seam one day earlier and its risks block says 'the honest next step is a per-path decision about refusal or a work item, and it is deliberately not in this change' — this ships both halves. The stock repair of the 22 existing rows is deliberately NOT in this submission.

edits.rationale: Stop inventing identity. When the fallback fires and the fragment declares no data-component, emit the section ALREADY TYPED as `adopted-fragment` with ContentData={"body": fragment}, rather than the "section" sentinel. The new component's template is exactly `{{.body}}` — the identity function — so its render reproduces the stored bytes and the row becomes genuinely regenerable, which makes every downstream check true rather than merely quiet. If the component row is absent at runtime, degrade to HONEST UNKNOWN (slot 'page-fragment', NULL component_id, no content_data) plus the Layer B item — never back to the sentinel. Refusing here instead was rejected: the fallback exists because returning zero sections leaves the page with no page_components at all, which makes the rerender skip it silently (the :1438-1452 comment), so a refusal would re-open the defect it was added for.

Narrow the positional rename where it is provably unsound, and NOT further. planned[Position-1] is a statement about the first planned section of a COMPOSED page; a whole-page blob that arrived as a single unidentifiable fragment is not that, ever, and hero being planned first on all 22 affected pages is what turns the sentinel into 'hero'. Sections carrying identityFromFallback are skipped. Positional enrichment for genuine multi-section extractions is left intact — it serves the alignment case it was built for, and deleting it wholesale would be a second defect.

The verification, at the seam. For each section with a resolved ComponentID, compare the component template's data-component value against the one in the section's HTML and flag when the template declares one and the HTML's value IS DISTINCT FROM it (absence counts — that is the whole pathological class, and `<>` returns a clean zero here because NULL is not false; the trap is in the lane RUNBOOK). NO verbatim exemption at this seam, and that is a reachability argument rather than an omission: a verbatim page is rebuild_policy='owned' by definition of the triple, and the owned-page guard at save_page_sections_action.go:186 refuses the whole save unconditionally, before every section-level guard (VERIFIED — a bare block immediately after the page lookup, whose own comment says it refuses 'rather than fall through to the heuristic guards below'). A copied-in exemption clause here would be dead code inviting a later reader to delete the real protection. The DETECTOR (edit 5) carries the exemption explicitly instead, sharing the canonical triple with loadVerbatimPageHTML rather than respelling it. REUSE, NOT ADDITION, on 342's pattern: the data-component extraction this whole plan rests on is already compiled inline TWICE in save_page_sections_action.go (:1392 and :1498, identical regex), and the guard plus detector would make four spellings in two languages — while the spellings must differ subtly (HTML side `[^"]+`, template side `[^"{]+`, so an interpolated attribute never counts as a declaration). One helper pair replaces both inline compilations and is used by the extractor, the enricher and the guard, with the SQL rendering generated from the same source on the interactiveHTMLSQL 'ONE definition, two languages' precedent (:1695-1710) and its parity test. Otherwise the enricher could adopt an identity the guard then refuses on a different reading of the same attribute. Report level is Error, by 342's own reasoning: Warn is the siblings' level for degraded-but-legitimate (a merely-empty optional field), Error for definitionally wrong (a dead URL control). Refuse-on-certainty only: the 190 of 339 components declaring no data-component are invisible to it, stated as a limit in the file rather than glossed.

Placement is the one thing this must not copy from its precedent. sectionIsUnresolvableStub skips inside the insert loop, AFTER the DELETE — correct for a hollow stub, because nothing of value is lost. Here the row holds the ONLY copy of a tool, so a post-DELETE skip would empty the page. The call therefore runs BEFORE the history snapshot and the DELETE, beside the claims/shrink/floor guards, honouring this file's own stated doctrine that 'a refused save writes nothing at all'. It runs AFTER the Layer 2 interactive carry-forward so it judges the FINAL bytes — which is precisely what breaks the conservation loop once armed, because the re-spliced hero-identity/tool-bytes section arrives at the seam already self-contradictory.

The seam guard only sees rows flowing through save_page_sections. Five other writers insert page_components (deploy_tool_action, create_tool_component_action, create_report_page_action, rebuild_blog_listing_action, adopt_verbatim) and this covers their output without touching any of them — the alternative being five edits that each depend on the author remembering. Files the SAME component_identity_mismatch item type as the seam; two producers of one type is blessed by the 2026-08-02 owner ruling provided the register entry names the producer set and the item_key shape, which it does. No automated repair route is wired, deliberately: auto-repairing identity is exactly the destructive-fix class bugs_closed/277 was nearly destroyed by. The seam and the detector deliberately ask DIFFERENT questions and their divergence is signal, stated at both sites so nobody 'fixes' one to match the other: the seam asks 'could the component I am about to bind have produced the bytes I am about to store?' (final post-carry-forward bytes, templates as at write time); the detector asks 'does this stored row still agree with its component's CURRENT self-declaration?' (rows at rest, templates as they are today). They legitimately diverge on template drift — a row written when the two agreed and flagged after the template's attribute changed is a STALE ROW, not a detector bug, and drift being the detector's legitimate secondary catch is the same property that made the static-prefix test wrong for the SEAM.

The component Layer A types rows as. function/name 'adopted-fragment', component_level='section', html_template EXACTLY '{{.body}}' so the render is the identity function and a stored fragment round-trips byte-for-byte; input_schema declares body as html/source:authored/required with guidance saying the value is a verbatim-adopted fragment that may contain scripts and must not be rewritten as prose. Deliberately NOT reusing 'ported-prose' (its schema forbids script-addressed elements — an invitation to rewrite live JS as prose) or 'ported-page' (site-specific to webdesign.co.uk). Applies BEFORE the Layer A image rolls: a seed naming a component the image does not yet use is inert, whereas an image typing rows against an absent component takes the honest-unknown degrade path.

commit af4743464 (bugs_open/342, 2026-08-21, the same seam one day earlier): 'REPORT ONLY, NO REFUSAL... Refusing at the seam would be new authority over content that renders successfully today at thirteen sites that never asked for it (owner ruling 2026-08-02 §2).' This submission follows that precedent: recording is unconditional, refusal is opt-in and seeded on nobody.
plan.risks:
WHY A REFUSAL ARM AT ALL, when 342 chose report-only at the adjacent seam one day ago — the objection I most expect, so I will argue it rather than assert it. What SHIPS here behaves exactly like 342: the field is seeded on nobody, so at roll time the seam records and files and refuses nothing. The difference is that the refusal exists in code, and three things separate the cases. (1) 342's predicate is a judgement about content quality — optional fields, fleet defaults like cta_text->'Get Started', schema-less components, thirteen sites rendering fine — so its refusal would have had false positives BY DESIGN. Ours is a certainty test: 1,550 agreements, 0 both-declared disagreements, 24 true positives, and every false positive falls in one structurally identifiable class. Refusing on certainty and refusing on suspicion are different acts. (2) 342's load-bearing second clause — 'the two paths that DO want to refuse already do, before the render' — has NO analogue here: there is no earlier gate for component identity anywhere, because the INSERT is the first point at which bytes, resolved component and template coexist. Copying 342's conclusion here means report-only FOREVER, which leaves the measured conservation loop (rerender -> Layer 2 splice -> re-mint) running with paperwork attached. (3) 342 was adding the FIRST refusal to a seam that had none — genuinely new authority. This action already refuses on claims (:596), shrink (:612), layout flatness (:633), completeness (:713) and ownership (:186); the new thing is only the predicate, and the 2026-08-02 field is what puts arming it in front of each caller's reviewer.

SCOPE, and I want the guardian seat to weigh it rather than have me assert it away. Layer A changes what a shared action PERSISTS — the identity of a row — inside a bug fix. Its defence is that the fallback's current output is measured wrong wherever it is testable (22 of 22) and unknowable otherwise, which is the argument against continuing to guess; the concept-register entry ships in the same commit (platform-seams condition 2); and the other consumers are named and will be told rather than merely measured (2026-07-29 ruling 3): tool-recreation-handler, page-build-handler, page-rebuild, page-rerender, site-work-orchestrator.

RFC_022: the opt-in field is opt-in, its UNSAFE side (today's behaviour — mislabelled rows persist) is the default, and zero live consumers name it, ENUMERATED above with a control rather than asserted. But I flag against my own interest that the sibling opt-in from RFC_010's worked example is also at zero consumers, i.e. this estate ships default-OFF switches and does not come back to arm them. If the council thinks record-only is therefore the honest permanent state, say so and I will drop the refusal arm rather than add a tenth inert key toward the N=10 budget.

OPTIONAL-KEY BUDGET: save_page_sections has no RegisterActionInputSpec, so a new key may enter the register counted as ZERO — the retract_asset_files/publish_site trap. The parity test cmd/config-key-audit/optional_budget_cron_parity_test.go must run, and the cron literal kept in step.

WRITE VOLUME on the fleet's busiest save path: the item is filed only on the mismatch condition and deduped on site:page:slot, bounding it at 27 keys fleet-wide today; it mirrors writeContentDataRegressionLog's record-never-refuse precedent in the same file.

KNOWN LIMIT, not a defect to be discovered later: adopted-fragment's {{.body}} template declares no data-component, so Layer B can never vouch for the rows Layer A types. The alternative — wrapping the fragment in a <section data-component=...> — changes served bytes on 22 live pages. Byte-preservation wins and the limit is registered.

OPEN AND NOT ASSUMED EITHER WAY: whether a full page rebuild THROUGH THE WRITER (as opposed to a rerender) ever renders the hero template over the tool. Rerender demonstrably does not. If such a path exists and bypasses save_page_sections, this guard does not cover it — that would be a separately filed producer, not a reason to widen this seam blind.

NOT IN THIS SUBMISSION: the stock repair of the 22 rows. It changes what four live sites serve, it is the owner's decision, and it must follow the Layer A roll or the producer re-mints a repaired page.
